name: Encephalitis

criteria.description: Altered mental status lasting ≥24 hours with no alternative cause identified
Fever ≥38°C within 72 hours before or after presentation
New onset of seizures not explained by a preexisting seizure disorder
Cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis (>5 white blood cells/mm³)
Brain MRI showing abnormalities consistent with encephalitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of altered mental status lasting ≥24 hours plus at least two additional criteria (fever, seizures, CSF pleocytosis, or brain imaging abnormalities)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of alternative causes such as metabolic or toxic encephalopathies.

searchTerms: recent onset of specific neurological symptoms

common.symptomName: Headache of moderate to severe intensity
Behavioral changes including agitation or psychosis
searchTerms: changes in behavior like agitation or psychosis
low blood pressure from autonomic dysfunction
hypotension due to nervous system instability
skin rash with viral brain infection

laboratory: Cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis with lymphocytic predominance
PCR detection of viral DNA/RNA in CSF (e.g., HSV, enteroviruses)
imaging: MRI brain showing hyperintense lesions on T2/FLAIR in temporal lobes or other affected regions
Possible contrast enhancement of affected brain areas
genetic: No specific genetic markers; some autoimmune encephalitis forms associated with HLA subtypes
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing diffuse slowing or epileptiform discharges
Brain biopsy rarely performed but may show inflammatory infiltrates

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant meningeal signs rather than brain parenchymal involvement
CSF findings with neutrophilic predominance in bacterial meningitis
MRI shows multifocal demyelinating lesions rather than viral encephalitis pattern
Progressive focal neurological deficits without fever
Imaging shows mass lesion with mass effect

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (e.g., papilledema, vomiting)
references: Granerod J, et al. Causes of encephalitis and differences in their clinical presentations in England: a multicentre, population-based prospective study. Lancet Infect Dis. 2010.
Venkatesan A, et al. Case Definitions, Diagnostic Algorithms, and Priorities in Encephalitis: Consensus Statement of the International Encephalitis Consortium. Clin Infect Dis. 2013.
Kennedy PGE. Viral encephalitis: causes, differential diagnosis, and management. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 2004.
